source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Fuel Tank and Exhaust Systems, p.8-5

procedures.title: Fuel gauge tank unit: test
steps: Do not test the tank unit by pushing a metal rod through the filler neck to move the float arm; the rod can spark against the tank lip or ground the gauge unit.
Instead, unplug the leads from the installed tank unit and connect them to a known-good tank unit outside the tank.

procedures.title: Fuel gauge tank unit (metering unit): remove and install
steps: Take the spare tire off the carrier.
Unbolt and remove the spare tire carrier.
Disconnect the fuel lines at the gauge unit.
Remove the cam lock with Tool J-8950.
Lift out the unit and its rubber gasket carefully so the screen on the pickup pipe end is not damaged.
Blow the strainer clean with compressed air.
Install in reverse order, always with a new gasket.
notes: When starting the cam lock, the gasket may need slight compression by pressing down on the tool; once the lock is under the retaining tangs, pressure can be released.

procedures.title: Fuel lines: routing
steps: Route the tank-to-pump fuel lines along the right frame rail.
Secure them to the frame or underbody with clamp-and-screw assemblies or riveted clips.
Use flexible hoses at the tank pickup and at the fuel pump (see figures 11-14 in the manual).
notes: Corvette uses a vented, anti-surge filler cap (no separate tank vent hoses).
